categories.main_business_segments: Campbell operates two primary reportable segments: Meals & Beverages and Snacks. The Meals & Beverages segment includes soups, simple meals, and beverages sold in the U.S. and Canada, as well as foodservice and select snacking products. The Snacks segment comprises cookies, crackers, bakery, and salty snack products, primarily in the U.S. retail market, and includes brands like Pepperidge Farm, Goldfish, Snyder’s of Hanover, and others. Recent acquisitions and divestitures, such as Sovos Brands and the sale of Pop Secret and noosa yoghurt, have shaped the current segment composition.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Campbell relies on large-scale food manufacturing, packaging, and distribution capabilities, with a focus on supply chain optimization and productivity improvements. The company uses a mix of company-owned and contract manufacturing facilities, advanced inventory management, and commodity risk management tools. Recent investments include network optimization, IT infrastructure upgrades, and wastewater treatment enhancements. Proprietary recipes, food processing know-how, and a robust trademark portfolio underpin product development.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Campbell’s primary customers are major retail food chains, mass merchandisers, club stores, convenience stores, dollar stores, and e-commerce platforms. The company also serves foodservice operators and commercial/non-commercial establishments. Its five largest customers account for about 47% of net sales, with Walmart alone representing 21%. Both segments sell to Walmart and other large retailers, and the company has a direct-store-delivery model for Snacks.
categories.geographic_coverage: Campbell is a North American-focused company, with approximately 95% of net sales generated in the U.S. and the remainder primarily in Canada and Latin America. The company operates manufacturing and distribution facilities across the U.S., with limited international operations. Beginning in 2026, Latin American retail business will be managed under the Meals & Beverages segment.
categories.supply_chain_position: Campbell operates primarily as a downstream manufacturer and marketer of branded consumer packaged foods and beverages. It sources ingredients and packaging from a broad supplier base, manages production and distribution, and sells finished goods to retailers and foodservice customers. The company also utilizes contract manufacturers and independent distributors, especially for its Snacks segment.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Campbell’s strategy centers on four pillars: building a top team, maintaining a best-in-class brand portfolio, executing with operational excellence, and making a lasting community impact. The company invests in consumer-focused marketing, product innovation, supply chain digitization, and sustainability initiatives. R&D efforts target new product development, process improvements, and adaptation to evolving consumer preferences, with a focus on health, wellness, and convenience.
categories.revenue_model: Campbell generates revenue primarily through the sale of branded food and beverage products to retailers, foodservice operators, and distributors. Revenue is recognized upon delivery of goods, net of trade promotions, discounts, and coupons. The Snacks segment also utilizes a direct-store-delivery model, and the company occasionally licenses brands or sells routes to independent distributors.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Campbell faces intense competition from large branded food and beverage companies, private label manufacturers, and emerging brands across all categories. Key competitors include Kraft Heinz, General Mills, Conagra, Kellogg, Mondelez, and private label/store brands. Campbell positions itself as a category leader in soups and select snack categories, emphasizing brand strength, innovation, and scale, but faces ongoing pressure from private label and retailer consolidation.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2025, Campbell reported net sales of $10.25 billion, up 6% year-over-year, driven by the Sovos Brands acquisition and an extra week in the fiscal year. Net earnings attributable to Campbell were $602 million, with a gross margin of 30.4%. The company has a moderate growth profile, with recent growth fueled by acquisitions, but faces margin pressures from inflation, tariffs, and supply chain costs. Capital expenditures were $426 million, and the company maintains significant debt following recent acquisitions.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Campbell emphasizes high-quality, trusted brands with strong consumer recognition, offering convenient, value-oriented meal and snacking solutions. The company differentiates through its iconic leadership brands, broad product portfolio, and focus on innovation, taste, and nutrition. Investments in supply chain efficiency, sustainability, and digital capabilities further support its value proposition to customers and consumers.
